--- title: "t-test" class-date: "Oct 22, 2026" --- **Class date:** {{< meta class-date >}}\ Based in part on lecture notes by Prof. Byoungkwan Lee and *이병관 (2023). 사회과학 연구자를 위한 R을 활용한 기초 통계. 한양대학교출판부.* # 4.2 단일표본 *t*-test **Exercise:** 생쥐 10마리의 몸무게 평균이 생쥐의 모집단 평균 몸무게 25g과 다른지를 95% 신뢰수준에서 검증해보자. - $H_{0}:\mu=25$ - $H_{A}:\mu\neq25$ ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(datarium) data(mice) ``` ::: ### STEP1. Check the normality assumption **(1) Visual inspection** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} hist(mice$weight, breaks=seq(10,30,by=1), col="grey", border="white", prob=T, ylim=c(0,0.3)) lines(density(mice$weight)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](t-test_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=672} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} library(ggpubr) ggqqplot(mice, "weight") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](t-test_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-2-2.png){width=672} ::: ::: **(2) Descriptive statistics** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(psych) describe(mice$weight) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` vars n mean sd median trimmed mad min max range skew kurtosis se X1 1 10 20.14 1.9 19.8 20.06 1.48 17.5 23.4 5.9 0.52 -1.08 0.6 ``` ::: ::: **(3) Test statistics** The null hypothesis of the Shapiro-Wilk test is *“there is no difference between the distribution of samples and the normal distribution.”* ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} shapiro.test(mice$weight) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Shapiro-Wilk normality test data: mice$weight W = 0.92295, p-value = 0.3822 ``` ::: ::: ### STEP2. Conduct *t*-test ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} t.test(mice$weight, mu = 25) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` One Sample t-test data: mice$weight t = -8.1045, df = 9, p-value = 1.995e-05 alternative hypothesis: true mean is not equal to 25 95 percent confidence interval: 18.78346 21.49654 sample estimates: mean of x 20.14 ``` ::: ::: ### STEP3. Report the result of *t*-test An one-sample *t*-test was conducted to investigate the difference between the sample data and the population. The assumption of normality based on Shapiro-Wilk normality test was met. The findings indicated that the sample data reported the lower level of weight (*M* = 20.14, *SD* = 1.9) than found in the population as a whole, *t*(9) = -8.1, *p* \< .001. ### Present the graphical results \[Optional\*\] ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(rstatix) stat.test <- mice %>% t_test(weight ~ 1, mu = 25) library(ggpubr) ggdensity(mice, x = "weight", rug = TRUE, fill = "lightgray") + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(15, 27)) + stat_central_tendency(type = "mean", color = "red", linetype = "dashed") + geom_vline(xintercept = 25, color = "blue", linetype = "dashed") + labs(subtitle = get_test_label(stat.test, detailed = TRUE)) + theme_classic() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](t-test_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: # 4.3 이표본 *t*-test *\*아래부터는 교재 141쪽 4.4 R을 이용한 분석 예제 섹션 참조* ## 4.4.1 독립표본 *t*-test **Exercise:** 인지부조화 이론의 유명한 실험 중 하나인 1달러-20달러 실험(Festinger & Carlsmith, 1959) 연구자들은 "1달러만 제공받은 집단이 20달러를 받은 집단에 비해 자신들이 참여한 실험에 대해 보다 호의적인 태도를 보일 것"으로 예측한다. 연구자들의 가설이 입증되었을까? 이를 α = .05에서 독립표본 *t*-test를 사용하여 검증해보자. - $H_{0}:\mu_{1d}=\mu_{20d}$ - $H_{A}:\mu_{1d}\neq\mu_{20d}$ ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} attitude <- c(3, 3, 4, 6, 5, 5, 5, 7, 8, 5, 4, 8, 2, 6, 4, 4, 6, 7, 5, 5, 1, 2, 5, 2, 3, 5, 4, 5, 2, 3, 4, 4, 1, 2, 3, 3, 5, 1, 1, 3) condition <- rep(c("$1", "$20"), c(20,20)) id <- seq(1:40) festinger <- data.frame(id, condition, attitude) ``` ::: ### STEP1. Check the normality assumption **(1) Visual inspection** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} festinger$condition <- as.factor(festinger$condition) library(gridExtra) p1 <- ggdensity(festinger, x = "attitude", add = "mean", rug = TRUE, color = "condition", fill = "condition", palette = c("#00AFBB", "#E7B800")) p2 <- ggqqplot(festinger, x = "attitude", color = "condition", palette = c("#00AFBB", "#E7B800"), shape = "condition") grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](t-test_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: **(2) Descriptive statistics** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(psych) describeBy(festinger$attitude, festinger$condition) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Descriptive statistics by group group: $1 vars n mean sd median trimmed mad min max range skew kurtosis se X1 1 20 5.1 1.62 5 5.06 1.48 2 8 6 0.13 -0.77 0.36 ------------------------------------------------------------ group: $20 vars n mean sd median trimmed mad min max range skew kurtosis se X1 1 20 2.95 1.43 3 2.94 1.48 1 5 4 0.08 -1.39 0.32 ``` ::: ::: **(3) Test statistics** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} by(festinger$attitude, festinger$condition, shapiro.test) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` festinger$condition: $1 Shapiro-Wilk normality test data: dd[x, ] W = 0.9571, p-value = 0.4876 ------------------------------------------------------------ festinger$condition: $20 Shapiro-Wilk normality test data: dd[x, ] W = 0.89825, p-value = 0.03825 ``` ::: ::: ### STEP2. Check the homogeneity of variance ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(car) leveneTest(festinger$attitude, festinger$condition) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Levene's Test for Homogeneity of Variance (center = median) Df F value Pr(>F) group 1 0.0281 0.8677 38 ``` ::: ::: ### STEP3. Conduct *t*-test & calculate effect size ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} t.test(attitude ~ condition, var.equal = T, data = festinger) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Two Sample t-test data: attitude by condition t = 4.4488, df = 38, p-value = 7.301e-05 alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group $1 and group $20 is not equal to 0 95 percent confidence interval: 1.171665 3.128335 sample estimates: mean in group $1 mean in group $20 5.10 2.95 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} library(effsize) cohen.d(festinger$attitude ~ festinger$condition) #biased ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Cohen's d d estimate: 1.406844 (large) 95 percent confidence interval: lower upper 0.6918574 2.1218315 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} cohen.d(festinger$attitude ~ festinger$condition, hedges.correction=T) #unbiased ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Hedges's g g estimate: 1.378894 (large) 95 percent confidence interval: lower upper 0.6808511 2.0769366 ``` ::: ::: ### STEP4. Report the result of *t*-test \**t*-test 결과 표는 그냥 워드에서 직접 만드는게 빠를 수도 있음 주의 ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(broom) library(kableExtra) model <- t.test(attitude ~ condition, var.equal = T, data = festinger) # tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE) %>% kable() %>% kable_styling() tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE) %>% select(!c(estimate, estimate1, estimate2, method, alternative)) %>% mutate(M.1 = mean(festinger$attitude[festinger$condition == "$1"]), SD.1 = sd(festinger$attitude[festinger$condition == "$1"]), n.1 = length(festinger$attitude[festinger$condition == "$1"]), M.2 = mean(festinger$attitude[festinger$condition == "$20"]), SD.2 = sd(festinger$attitude[festinger$condition == "$20"]), n.2 = length(festinger$attitude[festinger$condition == "$20"]), LB = conf.low, UB = conf.high, t = statistic, p = p.value, df = parameter, cohend = cohen.d(festinger$attitude ~ festinger$condition)$estimate, hedge = cohen.d(festinger$attitude ~ festinger$condition, hedges.correction = T)$estimate, .keep = "none") %>% kableExtra::kbl(caption = "Table 1. Result of t-test and Descriptive Statistics for the Cognitive Dissonance Experiment", col.names = c("M", "SD", "n", "M", "SD", "n", "LB", "UB", "t", "p", "df", "cohen's d", "hedges' g"), align = "c", digits = 2) %>% kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>% kableExtra::add_header_above(c("$1 group" = 3, "$20 group" = 3, "95% CI" = 2, " " = 5)) %>% kable_classic() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
Table 1. Result of t-test and Descriptive Statistics for the Cognitive Dissonance Experiment
$1 group
$20 group
95% CI
M SD n M SD n LB UB t p df cohen's d hedges' g
5.1 1.62 20 2.95 1.43 20 1.17 3.13 4.45 0 38 1.41 1.38
````` ::: ::: Using an alpha level of .05, a two-sample independent *t*-test was conducted to confirm the difference in attitude between the experimental conditions. Before conducting the test, assumption testings were performed. Normality was confirmed based on the Shapiro-Wilk normality test (*p* = .48 for group \$1 and *p* = .04 for group \$20), and homogeneity of variance was confirmed to satisfy based on the Levene’s test (*p* = .87). Altough the normality of group \$20 was not satisfied according to the Shapiro-Wilk normality test (*p* = .04), the author concluded that the normality of the data was acceptable based on visual inspections. As the Table 1 indicated, the result demonstrated that the attitude between \$1 group (*M*=5.1, *SD*=1.62) and \$20 group (*M*=2.95, *SD*=1.43) is statistically different, *t*(38) = 4.45, *p* \< .001, 95% CI \[1.17, 3.13\]. The effect size for this analysis was found as large (Cohen's *d* = 1.41, Hedges' *g* = 1.38). Therefore, according to the analysis results, we conclude that the minimal justification for behavior leads to cognitive dissonance, which has a statistically significant effect on attitude change. ## 4.4.2 대응표본 *t*-test **Exercise:** Baumann, Seifert-K essell, and Jones (1992)는 읽기-사고 활동(Directed Reading-Thinking Activity: DRTA)과 소리 내어 생각하기(Think Aloud: TA)와 같은 독서 수행전략이 학생들의 독해력 향상에 효과가 있는지를 실험을 통해 살펴보았다. 이들의 연구에서는 초등학교 4학년 66명의 학생들이 하나의 통제 집단과 두 처치 집단 DRTA 집단과 TA 집단 중 하나에 무작위로 배정되었다. 각 집단의 참가자들은 각각의 처치를 받은 후 독해력 테스트가 수행되었다. 독해력 테스트는 참가 학생들의 독서 오류율, 즉 독서 중에 얼마나 많은 오류가 있었는지를 통해 평가되었다. 예제 데이터 ‘reading.csv’에는 DRTA 전략 수행 전후의 독해력 테스트 점수를 담고 있다. 지금부터 DRTA 전략 수행이 학생들의 독해력 향상에 효과가 있었는지를 대응표본 t-test를 이용하여 확인해보자. - $H_{0}:\mu_{D}=\Delta_{0}$ - $H_{A}:\mu_{D}\neq\Delta_{0}$ ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} reading <- read.csv("data/reading.csv", header = T) differences <- reading$pretest - reading$posttest ``` ::: ### STEP1. Check the normality assumption **(1) Visual inspection** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} hist(differences, col="grey", border="white",prob=T) lines(density(differences)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](t-test_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-15-1.png){width=672} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ggqqplot(differences) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](t-test_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-15-2.png){width=672} ::: ::: **(2) Descriptive statistics** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(psych) describe(reading[,3:4]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` vars n mean sd median trimmed mad min max range skew kurtosis pretest 1 22 9.73 2.69 9 9.44 1.48 6 16 10 0.81 -0.40 posttest 2 22 6.23 2.09 6 6.33 1.48 0 11 11 -0.68 2.26 se pretest 0.57 posttest 0.45 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} describe(differences) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` vars n mean sd median trimmed mad min max range skew kurtosis se X1 1 22 3.5 3.25 3 3.44 3.71 -3 9 12 0.19 -0.82 0.69 ``` ::: ::: **(3) Test statistics** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} shapiro.test(differences) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Shapiro-Wilk normality test data: differences W = 0.95077, p-value = 0.3272 ``` ::: ::: ### STEP2. Conduct *t*-test & calculate effect size ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} t.test(reading$pretest, reading$posttest, paired = T) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Paired t-test data: reading$pretest and reading$posttest t = 5.0548, df = 21, p-value = 5.267e-05 alternative hypothesis: true mean difference is not equal to 0 95 percent confidence interval: 2.060046 4.939954 sample estimates: mean difference 3.5 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} #Pivot data from wide to long library(tidyr) reading.l <- reading %>% pivot_longer(cols = c(pretest, posttest), names_to = "Group", values_to = "reading.error") %>% select(-group) head(reading.l, 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 3 × 3 id Group reading.error 1 1 pretest 7 2 1 posttest 6 3 2 pretest 7 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} library(rstatix) reading.l %>% rstatix::cohens_d(reading.error ~ Group, paired=T) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1 × 7 .y. group1 group2 effsize n1 n2 magnitude * 1 reading.error posttest pretest -1.08 22 22 large ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} reading.l %>% rstatix::cohens_d(reading.error ~ Group, paired=T, hedges.correction=T) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1 × 7 .y. group1 group2 effsize n1 n2 magnitude * 1 reading.error posttest pretest -1.04 22 22 large ``` ::: ::: ### STEP3. Report the result of *t*-test \**t*-test 결과 표는 그냥 워드에서 직접 만드는게 빠를 수도 있음 주의 ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(broom) library(kableExtra) model <- t.test(reading$pretest, reading$posttest, paired = T) d <- reading.l %>% rstatix::cohens_d(reading.error ~ Group, paired=T) g <- reading.l %>% rstatix::cohens_d(reading.error ~ Group, paired=T, hedges.correction=T) tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE) %>% select(!c(estimate, method, alternative)) %>% mutate(M.1 = mean(reading$pretest), SD.1 = sd(reading$pretest), n.1 = length(reading$pretest), M.2 = mean(reading$posttest), SD.2 = sd(reading$posttest), n.2 = length(reading$posttest), LB = conf.low, UB = conf.high, t = statistic, p = p.value, df = parameter, cohend = d$effsize, hedge = g$effsize, .keep = "none") %>% kableExtra::kbl(caption = "Table 2. Result of t-test and Descriptive Statistics for Reading Ability by Directed Reading Activity", col.names = c("M", "SD", "n", "M", "SD", "n", "LB", "UB", "t", "p", "df", "cohen's d", "hedges' g"), align = "c", digits = 2) %>% kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>% kableExtra::add_header_above(c("Pre" = 3, "Post" = 3, "95% CI" = 2, " " = 5)) %>% kable_classic() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
Table 2. Result of t-test and Descriptive Statistics for Reading Ability by Directed Reading Activity
Pre
Post
95% CI
M SD n M SD n LB UB t p df cohen's d hedges' g
9.73 2.69 22 6.23 2.09 22 2.06 4.94 5.05 0 21 -1.08 -1.04
````` ::: ::: Using an alpha level of .05, a paired-sample *t*-test was conducted to examine the influence of *Directed Reading-Thinking Activity* (DRTA) on the average reading ability of pupils. Before the test, the normality was confirmed based on the Shapiro-Wilk normality test (*p* = .33). As the Table 2 indicated, the result demonstrated a statistically significant decrease in reading errors after exposure to DRTA (*M*=6.23, *SD*=2.09) compared to before DRTA (*M*=9.73, *SD*=2.69), *t*(21) = 5.05, *p* \< .001, 95% CI \[2.06, 4.94\]. The effect size for this analysis was large (Cohen's *d* = -1.08, Hedges' *g* = -1.04). Therefore, based on the analysis results, we can conclude that DRTA has a positive effect on reducing reading errors. # Cf. When assumptions are violated, what should be done? ### Normality \*The normality assumption is not a robust assumption. **Non-parametric method (e.g., Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test)** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} wilcox.test(festinger$attitude ~ festinger$condition, data = festinger) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction data: festinger$attitude by festinger$condition W = 333, p-value = 0.0002748 alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0 ``` ::: ::: **Robust *t*-test** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(WRS2) yuen(attitude ~ condition, data = festinger) #Yuen's test ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: yuen(formula = attitude ~ condition, data = festinger) Test statistic: 4.4486 (df = 21.98), p-value = 2e-04 Trimmed mean difference: 2.08333 95 percent confidence interval: 1.112 3.0546 Explanatory measure of effect size: 0.77 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} akp.effect(attitude ~ condition, data = festinger) #Robust Cohen's d ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` $AKPeffect [1] 1.532218 $AKPci [1] 0.6010449 2.2966200 $alpha [1] 0.05 $call akp.effect(formula = attitude ~ condition, data = festinger) attr(,"class") [1] "AKP" ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} yuenbt(attitude ~ condition, data = festinger, nboot = 5000) # Yuen's test bootstrapped ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: yuenbt(formula = attitude ~ condition, data = festinger, nboot = 5000) Test statistic: 4.5287 (df = NA), p-value = 0 Trimmed mean difference: 2.08333 95 percent confidence interval: 1.1074 3.0593 ``` ::: ::: ### Homogeneity of variance **Welch’s *t*-test** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} t.test(attitude ~ condition, data = festinger) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Welch Two Sample t-test data: attitude by condition t = 4.4488, df = 37.44, p-value = 7.48e-05 alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group $1 and group $20 is not equal to 0 95 percent confidence interval: 1.171185 3.128815 sample estimates: mean in group $1 mean in group $20 5.10 2.95 ``` ::: :::
